tasks.short: Coordinate and sign a regulatory submission pack

steps.what: Submit product, market and document ids
Mark document ids missing from the pack
Draft the cover note from those document ids

loop.input: document ids and the cover template
loop.output: cover draft that cites document ids only
loop.check: Every cited document id is on the submission request
loop.stop: Leave the paragraph blank and stop that section if there is no document id
loop.why_not_simpler: Cover wording changes by market and a fixed mail-merge cannot write it

steps.what: Comment on the scientific sections
Sign this regulatory submission version
File only the signed submission version

tasks.design: Project leads submit product id, market, change type and document ids on a {WORKFLOW} form, replacing the old {SPREADSHEET} list and the {EMAIL} chase. A check in {DOCS} marks missing ids, and a bounded cover note may cite only those ids. The specialist signs one version. Only that version is filed through {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packs were copied from the last project, and the document list lived in mail, so a draft could cite a file nobody had agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: The request can carry document ids, so the contents list and the cover note can be checked against that set.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a thin section is good enough for this market is still a judgement, and a filed pack is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides the pack is complete enough to sign, and can refuse to file it.

ambition.what: Sign or return a submission pack at each document freeze, not only when the portal date is close

tasks.altitude: The week moves from retyping contents lists to closing gaps and signing. The specialist can block a filing that has no signed version.

reach.task: Replace a document the pack check rejected
reach.learn: Which document ids are in the signed version and which rows are still blank

evidence.claim: In a mid-size European firm this task is mostly assembling documents and then signing. The portal step is short. The hard part is whether the pack is complete.

Digest [S14] says a regulatory-information product tracks registrations and publishes submissions. That supports a versioned pack and a publish of a signed version, not an unattended scientific review.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the cover note may cite only document ids already on the request.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed submission version is filed or the specialist refuses it. Negotiating the science inside a section is out of scope.

Input contract: product id, market, change type, document id, document version, owner. Producer is the project lead. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.

The meeting share in the prior is small. Time today sits on the documents, the mailbox and the portal, not on a long meeting. Test native {DOCS} templates, {WORKFLOW} forms and the approval flow before any custom code.
unknowns: Which portal this firm must use, and for which markets.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
Which document types are mandatory for a given change type.
research_questions: What share of packs are missing a document id at first check?
How often does the signed version differ from the draft cover note?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits a cover note that cites a weak section
Specialist sign-off time on the pack stays in this step

incremental.description: Revise the cover template when a new market section is added
Project leads replace a document id the check rejects

approvals.approved_version: submission version signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many packs still arrive as mail with no document ids, so the specialist rebuilds the list by hand. The high case assumes the form is used but every pack still gets a full sign-off. The scientific rewrite of a section is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare an agency exchange and hold the conversation

steps.what: Log the agency question and its due date
Draft a briefing from the signed file

loop.input: question log and signed submission documents
loop.output: briefing that cites document ids only
loop.check: Every citation is a document id on the signed submission or the question log
loop.stop: Drop any sentence with no document id and stop after one draft
loop.why_not_simpler: The pathway wording is not a field stored on the question

steps.what: Supply a missing technical fact
Approve the reply line for this question
Hold the regulatory exchange with the agency reviewer
Write what was said and what is still open

tasks.design: The agency thread stays in {EMAIL}. The specialist logs question id, due date and topic on a {WORKFLOW} form. A briefing in {DOCS} may cite only the signed submission and that question. The specialist approves one reply line, then speaks or writes it. This task does not post anything to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrived as free text in mail, so a reply could not show which signed file it relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: The question and the signed submission can share an id, so a briefing can be limited to those documents.
tasks.still_hard: A live call can move past the written line, and the relationship with the agency reviewer is not a template.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses the pathway and the words said to the agency reviewer.

ambition.what: Approve a reply line when the question arrives, instead of holding every point for a monthly call

tasks.altitude: Preparation gets shorter. The specialist still holds the exchange and can refuse a line that the file does not support.

reach.task: Supply the technical fact the question names
reach.learn: Which questions already have an approved reply line and which are still open

evidence.claim: The agency exchange itself stays with the specialist. Only the briefing and the note of what was said can be prepared from the file.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so a briefing may not cite a document the signed file does not contain.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task runs from an inbound agency question to a note of what was said. Filing a formal response pack is a separate task.

Input contract: question id, received date, due date, topic, signed submission id, document id. Producer of the question is the agency thread in the mailbox. Producer of a missing fact is the project lead. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.

Meetings are a real part of this task, unlike routine document work. Mail replies with no call are the same exchange step. Test the native mailbox filing and {DOCS} template before any custom code. No machine sends the reply.
unknowns: Whether this firm answers agencies by mail, by call, or both.
Who may approve a reply line when the specialist is absent.
Which topics the project lead is allowed to answer.
research_questions: What share of agency questions are closed by mail with no call?
How often does the spoken reply go beyond the approved line?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the briefing before approving the line
Time on the agency exchange stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep question-log fields aligned with new request types
Project leads correct a fact the specialist rejected

approvals.approved_version: reply line approved for this question id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most questions are still unstructured mail, so the briefing rarely cites a clean document id and the specialist still prepares by hand. The high case assumes a clean log but every exchange and every reply line stays with the specialist. Nothing spoken is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Accept each new rule record into the knowledge base

steps.what: Collect new guidance titles from the source list
Propose one rule record per source document

loop.input: source text and the rule-record template
loop.output: one proposed record with citation and date
loop.check: The citation and the date both appear in the source text
loop.stop: Leave the record blank and stop if either is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: A summary of what changed is not a field on the source

steps.what: Mark which products the rule might touch
Accept or reject each rule record
Publish only the accepted rule record

tasks.design: A configured source list supplies title, date and link into a {WORKFLOW} queue, instead of a {SPREADSHEET} of bookmarks from {EMAIL}. A bounded pass proposes one rule record in {DOCS} and leaves it blank when the citation or the date is not on the source. The specialist accepts or rejects each record. Only an accepted record is published for others to read.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was saved as loose files and a list of links, so a later reader could treat an unreviewed note as current.
tasks.enabler_now: Sources that expose a title and a date can be queued as fields, and a record can be accepted or rejected as a unit.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding that a guidance document applies to this firm's products is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts or rejects each rule record. A rejection is not shown as current.

ambition.what: Accept or reject a new guidance item in the week it appears, not at a quarterly read

tasks.altitude: Collecting titles takes less time. The specialist's week is the accept or reject decision, and they can keep a record unpublished.

reach.task: Mark which products a new rule might touch
reach.learn: Which rule records are accepted and which were rejected

evidence.claim: Keeping a knowledge base is mostly collecting public guidance and deciding whether it applies. The hard part is applicability, not the copy.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so a proposed rule record must show a citation and a date that are on the source.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when a rule record is accepted or rejected. Advising a project from that record is a later task.

Input contract: source id, title, date, link, citation text, product ids the rule might touch. Producer of the source row is the configured source list. Producer of product ids is the product owner. A source with no title or no date stays on a manual list and is not proposed.

The model prior is real for the change summary only. Title and date are a fixed read. Test the native {DOCS} list and {WORKFLOW} queue before any custom code. This design does not watch staff reading habits.
unknowns: Which public sources belong on the source list.
Who may accept a record when the specialist is absent.
How product ids are named in the portfolio.
research_questions: How many new guidance items appear in a typical month?
What share of proposed records are rejected as out of scope?

already_counted.description: Specialist corrects a proposed record before deciding
Accept or reject time stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a source to the list and retire a dead one
Product owners correct a product id on a rejected scope

approvals.approved_version: rule record accepted or rejected in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many sources have no title or date, so the specialist still reads them by hand and the proposal rarely fires. The high case assumes clean sources but every record still needs an accept or reject. Reading time on a rejection is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review an adverse reaction and file the signed report

steps.what: Log the reaction case on the form
Flag case fields the report still needs
Draft the regulatory report from completed case fields

loop.input: completed case fields and the case notes
loop.output: report draft that restates those sources only
loop.check: Every event sentence appears in the case notes or a form field
loop.stop: Leave the narrative blank and stop if a sentence has no source span
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative wording is not a mail-merge of the coded fields alone

steps.what: Sign the report version and the seriousness
File only that signed report version
Hold a case that is not ready to file

tasks.design: Quality reviewers log case id, product id, event date, reporter type and the stated seriousness on a {WORKFLOW} form. Notices that still arrive by {EMAIL} are typed into that form, not left on a {SPREADSHEET}. A draft in {DOCS} fills the report only from those fields and the case notes, and stops when a required field is blank. The specialist signs one version, including the seriousness call. Only that version is filed through {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cases were retyped from mail into the report, so a narrative could add a detail that was not in the case.
tasks.enabler_now: The case form has fields the draft can check, and the portal can receive one identified version.
tasks.still_hard: Seriousness and whether the case is reportable can affect people, and a filed report is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist makes the seriousness call and signs the only version that may be filed.

ambition.what: Clear each new reaction case on the day it is logged, instead of in a weekly batch

tasks.altitude: Assembly of the report takes less time. The specialist keeps the seriousness call and can hold a case that is not ready.

reach.task: Correct a case field the report check rejected
reach.learn: Which cases are signed for filing and which are held

evidence.claim: Most of the time goes into fitting a case to the report layout. Whether it is reportable, and how serious it is, stays a person call. The draft must not add an event that is not in the case notes.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the reaction report may not cite a document that is not on the case.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when a signed report version is filed or the case is held. The firm's reporting clock is not assumed here.

Input contract: case id, product id, event date, reporter type, seriousness as stated, outcome code, country of occurrence. Producer is the quality reviewer. If a required field is empty the draft stops, the specialist does not sign a narrative, and the case stays on the hold list. Free-text medical history is not copied into a new field.

Access to the case form is the specialist and the quality reviewer. Test the native {WORKFLOW} form, {DOCS} template and approval flow before any custom code. A machine may file only the signed version.
unknowns: What reporting clock and which portal this firm must use.
Who may sign a report when the specialist is absent.
Whether the case form needs a separate privacy review.
research_questions: What share of cases are held for a missing field?
How often is a filed report corrected after the portal accepts it?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the report narrative before signing
Seriousness decision and signature stay with the specialist

incremental.description: Update the required-field list when the firm changes the report
Quality reviewers correct a case field the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: reaction report version signed with the seriousness call
the same signed reaction report version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many notices still arrive as unstructured mail, so the specialist retypes fields and the draft rarely completes. The high case assumes a complete form but every seriousness call and every signature stays with the specialist. Cases that are held are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist stops retyping packs, rule notes and report layouts, and keeps the week for agency conversations, seriousness calls and the versions they will sign.
reach: Project leads receive the signed submission version instead of a loose set of files.
Product owners can read which rule records were accepted and which were rejected.
Quality reviewers see which reaction cases were filed and which are still held.
skills_to_grow: Tie every submission citation to a document id on the request.
Keep an agency reply to the signed line before anything is sent or said.
Accept a rule record only when the citation and the date are on the source.
Sign a reaction report before any portal filing, and hold a case that is incomplete.
role.ambitious_version: Each submission and each reaction report that leaves the firm is a version the specialist signed, and each new guidance item is either an accepted rule record or a rejection.
